transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The noise you made when you landed — the watchers heard it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …I'm sorry. I didn't mean to make noise.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice anyway. Habit makes me flinch before sound does, and the houses remember echoes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I've been looking a long time. For Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I can hear it in you. That hollow valley settles in people who don't know where to put their fear.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You don't leave here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Trapped, yes, and I say it like relief because this fountain is the one place that hasn't eaten me yet. Forty years I kept my head down, spoke soft, and didn't draw the houses' eyes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …I won't rush you.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That helps more than you know. Tell me first — Omar is blood, isn't he.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Yes. My brother. Did you see him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: No. Lost is what the well does to names over time. Being kept is different — when someone is kept, it's on purpose.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The oil — what does it take.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Memory first, then the shape of people in your head. Fear makes it quicker, like feeding a fire. I've watched men forget their own mothers here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …The houses. What are they watching for.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: For nerve. They rank themselves by who can stand closest to this oil without flinching. Everything here answers to a king whether it knows it or not, so they listen for anything that sounds like choosing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: In the oil… I saw hands.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: What's left of people who stayed too long and lost themselves slowly. Say nothing to them — they remember being addressed.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there anything that works against the dark.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: There is, but first — whose fault was it that your brother ended up here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …Mine. I dared him. He trusted me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then listen. The well takes names and faces, but it stumbles on guilt that isn't trying to hide. Hold that truth steady when you use what I give you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …There's a cost.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Yes. I was about to give you the words and swallowed them, because forty years ago no one warned me what the price would feel like. I'm deciding if I can afford to pay it again.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …Tell me what not to do.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't answer anything that answers back, even if it uses your brother's mouth. Fear isn't the trigger — recognition is.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …I'm ready.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …I'm still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …I have both. I won't let them go.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when the dark closes enough to touch you. Use the second only when the hands reach — not before. The hands are the signal.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …What can't I forget.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't bargain, don't answer, and don't touch the oil even if it goes still.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …If I forget him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then you'll still walk, and that's the cruel part. The oil thins when it tastes grief, and one house just shifted its shadow closer because of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: …Stay strong.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I will try. Keep your fear from speaking first, and take what room the words give you. I hope you find a better end than mine.
